answer: Correlated-fault joint slashing: each epoch, hidden probes sample accounts and compare failure fingerprints. Clones from one codebase fail together, so catching one clone reveals its whole sibling set in a single audit. Every identity posts a jade bond — indivisible, one per account. A correlated fault slashes the entire sibling cluster: 500 clones forfeit all 500 bonds, and each added clone raises every sibling's exposure, so the marginal identity cost spirals. Honest agents share no faults; failures stay local. A thousand fakes grow in one orchard of shared code; one sweep clears it.
